summary: Made tokenizer-side cancellation the streaming visibility boundary: queued nonterminal chunks are dropped after abort dispatch, and the terminal abort event cannot expose accumulated text or token IDs.

tests.what_was_measured: The queued post-cancellation chunk was yielded immediately; the regression expected it to remain blocked until the abort acknowledgement.
29 tokenizer-manager unit tests and 3 subtests passed, including cancelled non-incremental streaming, incremental coalescing, and the uncancelled-stream boundary.
On the unmodified source, the real gfx950 server returned a post-cancel abort event for grammar_primary with output_ids [0]; the overlap peer continued.
With the fix, the real gfx950 server returned only an empty-text, empty-output_ids abort event for grammar_primary; the overlap peer continued.
Changed production and evidence scripts compile successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 ran the source-checkout SGLang server twice. Raw commands, server logs, request events, and process cleanup metadata are under reports/j-a3f881b2090a/evidence/.

remaining_limitations: The source report's meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct weights were unavailable.

The qualified tiny fixture lacks JSON punctuation, so XGrammar reported Accepted tokens: [] and token 0 decoded to empty text. The GPU run proves post-cancel token-ID visibility and its removal, not model semantic accuracy or the exact visible invalid string.
The reported dual RTX 4090 CUDA environment was not available; testing used one assigned gfx950 GPU and does not claim a multi-GPU reproduction.
